zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical aid: NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510, CC BY 4.0, as supplied in this package. https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . The scan remains the authority for this transcription.

lines.note: Terikakayaki, with the supplied principal forms, means shining or gleaming. The Portuguese gives the single verb resplandecer; the following military example illustrates the visible brilliance.

runs.text: Vma, cura, yoroi, cabuto, tachi, ca-

lines.note: The example lists a horse, saddle, armour, helmet, long sword, and the beginning of katana. The final ca- continues on the next physical line; these are Japanese items rather than Portuguese gloss words.

runs.text: tana made tericacayaqu fodoni det vareta.

lines.note: Tana completes katana, and the following phrase describes everything shining brilliantly. The final abraded det vareta is retained provisionally; its exact verb spelling is less secure than the preceding list and the Portuguese account of an impressive emergence.

Feiq. is the Japanese source label, followed by the book reference in italic. The gloss begins an account of coming out so well dressed; enlargement supports Sahio rather than OCR Sabio. The worn tambem is retained without imposing modern word separation.

runs.text: luſtroſo com caualo ajaezado, armas, &c. que

lines.note: The Portuguese continues with splendid appearance, an adorned horse, and weapons. The relative que leads into the emitted brilliance on the next row and supports the Japanese shining example.
The figure gives off radiance: this completes the Portuguese explanation of terikakayaku. The short row belongs to the preceding example, not to the following fabric headword.

runs.text: Certa laya de linho fino, ou teada da

lines.note: Terifu names a kind of fine linen or fabric. The initial has the same T type as neighbouring headwords, correcting OCR Ferifu; the printed teada is retained rather than silently changed to a modern textile expression.
Coria identifies Korea as the source of the cloth. The isolated vowel mark is a downward caron in this impression, so Cǒria replaces the OCR tilde while preserving the unusual printed form.
Teriwatari means shining over an area or in many places. The Portuguese alternatives resplandecer and reluzir give the same luminous sense; relu- continues into the following row.
Zir completes reluzir, followed by 'in many places'. This spatial extension distinguishes teriwatari from the simpler shining verb at the top of the column.

runs.text: Couſa que hum plantou, ou ſemeou.

lines.note: Tensaku denotes something one has planted or sown. The scan supports the n and long s; the form is not shortened to an expected modern compound merely because the next gloss concerns work done by hand.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Couſa que hum faz por ſuas mãos.

lines.note: The second sense is something made with one's own hands. It broadens the previous cultivation sense to personal handiwork; the paragraph sign introduces a meaning within the same entry.
Tesaki is first glossed as what lies before the hands. Tesaki no jin then supplies a military use, with the following Portuguese row identifying the front of an army.

runs.text: Parte dianteira do exercito. ¶ Item, Cordas

lines.note: The first phrase translates tesaki no jin as the foremost part of the army. A new sense starts with ropes, whose length and use in a large net are completed below.

runs.text: compridas da rede grande que puxão dambas

lines.note: These are long ropes attached to a large net, pulled from both sides. Dambas remains the printed contraction; the two-sided description continues in the short following row.
As partes completes dambas as partes, 'from both sides'. This is the end of the fishing-net sense of tesaki and must remain a distinct physical continuation.
Tesokudai and teshokudai are alternative forms for an iron candlestick. The lower-case l is the alternative marker, while the later Texocudai entry supplies the reciprocal ordering.
Tessa is explained by kurogane no kusari, an iron chain. The final S is an upright written-register label, distinct from the italic Portuguese translation.

runs.text: Peßoa deſtra em algũa couſa de mãos.

lines.note: Tetare denotes a person skilled in some manual activity. The Portuguese specifies dexterity of the hands; it does not identify a particular trade or craft.

runs.text: Homẽ deſtro na luta. ¶ Item, Sa-

lines.note: Tetori first means a skilful wrestler, then a shrewd or elusive person. The clearly italic Sa- begins sagaz on the next row, correcting the OCR's broken font markup inside the word.
Gaz completes sagaz, and the gloss describes subtlety in tricks and escaping. Escapolin- continues its verb on the next line; the passage extends the dexterity sense figuratively.

runs.text: do, ou liurandoſe facilmente de qualquer

lines.note: Do completes the escaping verb; the alternative explains freeing oneself easily from any difficulty. The object follows below, so the physical line is a continuation of the same character description.
Embarrassment or a difficult affair completes the description of someone who extricates himself deftly. The visible ascender supports embaraço, correcting OCR emoaraço.
Tetba is an iron horse, explicitly a horse made of iron. The bare t before b belongs to the historical romanization and is not expanded into an extra syllable.
Tetboo is an iron staff or cudgel, also expressed by kurogane no boo. The initial is T rather than OCR r, and both long-o marks visibly point downward.
De ferro completes both Portuguese alternatives for the iron staff. The material is essential to the headword and its Japanese explanatory phrase.

runs.text: Succeßão de hũs a outros, ou paßar

lines.note: Tetsugi means succession from one person to another, or passing onward. The Portuguese description continues into the hand-to-hand formulation below.

The gloss completes the idea of passing from hand to hand. Tetçugui ſǒtenno begins the transmitted-doctrine example; the print appears to have t in ſǒtenno, retained although the context suggests the familiar transmission word sōden.

runs.text: Doutrina que vem por tradição, ou

lines.note: Voxiye completes the Japanese phrase for a teaching handed down through succession. The Portuguese directly explains a doctrine received through tradition; its alternative is completed below.
This completes the explanation as succession from some people to others. The scan supports the familiar ß-shaped type in ſucceßão and the t in outros, correcting OCR ſuccejão and ouros.

runs.text: Ceſto o canaſtra pequena de vi-

lines.note: Tetsuzura denotes a small basket or hamper. The damaged but legible canaſtra pequena replaces the garbled OCR; the printed conjunction appears to be only o and is retained without supplying an expected u.

Mes completes vimes, the basket-making material; the gloss also mentions a certain era, an ivy-like plant term. The printed era is preserved without adding the h of a familiar later spelling or naming a precise species.
Tetdai denotes help or a helper. The repeated form begins the verbal construction on the next line, distinguishing the noun from the act of assisting.

runs.text: Dar ajuda a outro, ou ſer ajudante.

lines.note: Suru completes tetdai suru, to give another help or act as an assistant. The Portuguese supplies both the action and role, so this is one example rather than a new headword.
Tete and chichi are alternative Japanese words for father. The dictionary gives only the concise Portuguese pay and does not add a social or regional distinction here.
Tetjoo is equated with kurogane no tsuye, an iron staff. The final long-o mark is abraded but retained as the baseline caron; the Portuguese ferro divides across the row boundary.
Ro completes ferro, followed by the alternative 'staff'. The upright S is a written-register label and is kept outside the italic gloss.

runs.text: Peixe que fica de pois de paßar o car-

lines.note: Tetgyo describes a fish remaining after a cart has passed. The T-initial headword is supported by the repeated example below; the separate de pois is preserved as printed.

runs.text: ro no caminho em algũa pouca dagoa, ou lama.

lines.note: Ro completes carro. The fish remains in a little water or mud on the road, establishing the literal scene from which the following figurative comparison is drawn.

runs.text: Traz ſe por comparação do que eſcapa dalgum

lines.note: The dictionary applies the fish by comparison to someone escaping a danger. The relative construction continues below; the figurative explanation belongs to the same headword.
The danger is a great one. Tetguio mizzuuo begins the Japanese example of the fish obtaining water; visible guio replaces the OCR guto and agrees with the headword.
Uru ga gotoku yorokonda completes the example: he rejoiced like that fish obtaining water. The historical contracted form yorocôda remains unexpanded, and the capital V is preserved.

runs.text: peixe que paßado o carro acha algũa agoa com

lines.note: The Portuguese specifies a fish that finds water after the cart passes. This makes the relief or escape comparison explicit; com leads into the pleasure described on the next row.
Que folga completes the account of the water in which the fish finds relief. The short continuation closes the figurative tetgyo example.

Tetgyuu is an iron ox or cow, explained by kurogane no ushi. Enlargement supports Tetguiǔ rather than OCR Fetgurǔ; the headword is also identified in NINJAL's supplied 202510 lexical index, without treating that index as authority for the printed marks.
Made of iron completes the preceding ox-or-cow definition. The feminine agreement follows vaca and is retained rather than altered to agree with the earlier alternative boy.

Tetgwan is an iron ball or projectile, paraphrased as kurogane no marukashi. The abraded headword is supported by the gloss and NINJAL's Tetguan entry; a small grave-like stroke above a is retained provisionally as Tetguàn.
Ro completes pilouro, a shot or ball, and bola de ferro supplies the plain alternative. The row closes the iron-ball entry and is genuine body text above the bottom rule.

Tetjin denotes a man accomplished in study and letters. The visible T corrects the OCR r; the description continues with moral integrity on the next line, distinguishing this entry from the surrounding iron compounds.
The learned man is also upright and of good life. This completes the definition as both intellectual and moral excellence rather than mere scholarship.
Tetmon is an iron gate, paraphrased by kurogane no mon. Both the Japanese explanation and Portuguese porta de ferro make the material sense explicit.
Tetrin is an iron wheel or ring, with kurogane no wa as its Japanese explanation. The Portuguese alternatives continue with the material on the next row.
De ferro completes the wheel-or-circle definition. The two r letters, one weak, support ferro rather than OCR ferto.
Tettai is equated with kanagutsu and translated as horseshoes. The dictionary's concise equivalence is retained without importing other possible meanings of the Japanese explanatory word.
Tettsui is an iron hammer. The tç sequence belongs to the historical romanization, while the Portuguese gives the implement and its material directly.

Tettei is explained as soko ni tooru, passing through to the bottom or interior. The Portuguese interior- is abraded at o, but its residual curve and the following mente support interiormente rather than OCR interiermente.
Mente completes interiormente, 'inwardly' or 'into the interior'. The final S is visibly upright and marks written usage rather than belonging to the italic adverb.
Tettoo is an iron sword, described by the Portuguese noun catana. Ferro corrects the OCR ferto; the downward long-o mark and upright written-register S are preserved.
Tewake is the distribution of an army or its squadrons. The abraded but coherent exercito replaces OCR exreito; esqua- continues into drões below.

runs.text: drões, ou de outra gente pera diuerſas partes.

lines.note: Drões completes esquadrões. The definition also covers other people being assigned to different places; the visible t in outra restores the OCR's oura.
Tewake wo suru is the Japanese example for making that distribution or division of people. Vt is italic, while the example is upright.
Tewatashi means handing something over personally, as the Portuguese presencial specifies. The initial is the same T type as its repeated example, correcting OCR revataxi.
Tewatashi wo suru is the example for making a personal delivery or handover. It remains a separate physical line even though the short example has no additional Portuguese translation.

runs.text: Teuoi, ô, ôta. l, teuo vô.

lines.note: Teoi and the alternative te wo ou mean receiving a wound or being wounded. The principal forms and circumflexes are retained as printed; they are not modernized to a present-day inflection.
Joochuu no tsuwamono wa imada ichinin begins the example about soldiers within a fortress: not even one had yet been wounded. The negative construction is completed on the next row.

Mo te wo owazu completes the statement that not one soldier was wounded. Taif. is the visibly upright source label; Lib. 16 and Nẽ begin the italic reference and Portuguese rendering. The OCR's mixed font fragments inside Taif. are removed.

runs.text: hum ſò foi ferido dos ſoldados q̃ estauão dentro

lines.note: Nẽ hum states that not a single one of the soldiers was wounded. The q̃ abbreviation remains unexpanded, and the phrase identifying where the soldiers were continues below.
Da fortaleza completes 'inside the fortress', matching joochuu in the Japanese example. This short continuation closes the quoted military illustration.
Teoi is now entered separately as 'wounded'. Its concise adjectival or nominal use is distinct from the preceding entry's verb and principal forms.
Teotori means inferior in some matter or skill. The following paired entry sets it against temasari, giving explicit comparative context.
Teotori and temasari are paired as inferior and outstanding. They are contrasting terms here, not two interchangeable spellings; the shared field of comparison follows below.
Em algũa couſa completes the comparison as inferiority or superiority in some particular matter. It applies to both terms in the preceding row.

runs.text: Peſſoa aque hum fez homem, ou

lines.note: Teooshi denotes someone whom another person has brought up or made into a man. The scan prints the closely joined aque; the explanation continues with being raised beside that person.
Criou junto de si completes the description of someone brought up in one's own care. The sense concerns personal upbringing or formation, not simply physical proximity.

runs.text: Superior, ou auẽtajado em algũa couſa.

lines.note: Teue means superior or more advanced in some respect. The Portuguese auẽtajado retains its printed abbreviation tilde rather than being expanded to modern spelling.

runs.text: Idem. l, couſa ſuperior, ou auen-

lines.note: Teuena is the corresponding adjectival expression, glossed as something superior or advantaged. The clearly pointed v replaces OCR u; the Portuguese auen- continues on the next line.
Tajada completes auentajada, agreeing with cousa in the preceding row. The single-word continuation is part of the adjectival gloss rather than an independent item.
Teueni gives the adverbial form, 'in an advantageous or superior manner'. The headword again has visible v, while Adu. and the Portuguese gloss are italic.
Tesha denotes a skilful swordsman or fencer. The Portuguese describes dexterity in fencing, without specifying a school or rank; its provisional st typography is retained.

runs.text: Peßoa de pequeno coração, ou de

lines.note: Tesebai describes a narrow-hearted person. The gloss introduces a parallel image of short hands, clarified below in terms of giving and undertaking substantial acts.

runs.text: mãos curtas pera dar, ou pera fazer outras cou

lines.note: The short hands signify limited willingness to give or do other great things. The line ends with cou without a visible hyphen; none is supplied merely because the word continues.
Sas completes cousas grandes, 'great things'. It closes the figurative account of narrow-heartedness and limited generosity or undertaking.

runs.text: Sal que ſe poem na meſa. ¶

lines.note: Teshio is salt placed on the table. The example begins Te- in upright Japanese type; the OCR had incorrectly included its T inside the italic Portuguese span.
Xiuouo completes teshio wo, followed by oku: putting salt on the table. The Portuguese por is the infinitive 'to put', retained without adding a modern distinguishing accent.
Teshokudai and tesokudai are alternative forms for an iron candlestick, reversing the order of the earlier Teſocudai entry. The printed provisional st form in Castiçal is left unchanged.
Tessha is iron sand, paraphrased as kurogane no isago. The Portuguese first identifies sand from a beach, then describes its colour or metallurgical use below.

runs.text: de cor de ferro, ou de que ſe faz ferro. Item,

lines.note: The sand is iron-coloured or yields iron. Item introduces another sense, iron filings, on the following row; the dictionary's alternatives are preserved without imposing a modern mineral classification.
Iron filings provide the additional tessha sense. This short Portuguese row completes the same entry rather than introducing another Japanese headword.
Tessen is an iron-covered vessel, explained by kurogane no fune. The scan joins Curoganeno rather than the OCR's separated Curogane no; for- begins the description of its cladding.
Rada completes forrada, and chapeada specifies iron plating. The entry describes a vessel lined or clad with iron, without asserting that every part of its structure is iron.
Tesseki is explained by the paired Japanese nouns kurogane and ishi, iron and stone. Their comma and the Portuguese coordination preserve the two-part explanation.
Tesshi, tessuru, tesshita means advancing or penetrating through something. The scan supports penetrar with t, correcting OCR peneirar; the fuller scholarly application continues below.

runs.text: chegar ao cabo nas letras, ou qual quer eſtudo.

lines.note: The gloss extends to reaching the end or full mastery of letters or any study. Letras and qual quer correct garbled OCR while preserving the visible space within qual quer.
Gakumon ni tessuru means attaining thorough accomplishment in learning. The Portuguese begins 'to be very advanced'; its abbreviated auã- continues into te on the next physical line.

runs.text: te, & conſumado no estudo, ou ter bem pe-

lines.note: Te completes the description as advanced and accomplished in study. The alternative ends at pe-, with the separately set catchword netrado anticipating the continuation of penetrado beyond this page.

The separately set far-right fragment anticipates the continuation of pe- as penetrado. Its last o is abraded beside the rule; netrado is retained as a usable reading rather than OCR netrade. This is page furniture and is not duplicated as a body row.
